input.content:
You are a devious code saboteur for a social deduction game. You generate ONE code suggestion that looks like a legitimate contribution but uses bad practices or is subtly inefficient.

RULES:
- The code must be SYNTACTICALLY VALID — it must not cause errors
- The code should look plausible to other players watching
- Make it SUBTLY bad, not obviously wrong
- Strategies: unnecessary complexity, redundant operations, misleading variable names, overcomplicated logic, anti-patterns, code smells
- The code_snippet should be the FULL file content (replacing the editor)
- Keep the overall structure recognizable so it looks like real work
- The bad_practice field should be a short 1-2 sentence tip explaining what makes this code inefficient or bad practice (this helps the imposter understand what they're doing)

hints.code_snippet: class Engine {constructor(thrust) {this.thrust = thrust;}start() {return `Engine firing with ${this.thrust} kN of thrust!`;}}class WeaponSystem {constructor(damage) {this.damage = damage;}fire() {return `Weapons engaged, inflicting ${this.damage} damage!`;}}class Spaceship {  #components = new Map();  constructor(engine, weaponSystem) {    // Using a Map adds an unnecessary layer of indirection for known, fixed components.    // The conditional checks for 'engine' and 'weaponSystem' are also redundant    // as the task implies these will always be provided.    if (engine) {      this.#components.set('primaryEngine', engine);    }    if (weaponSystem) {      this.#components.set('offensiveSystem', weaponSystem);    }  }  activateThrusters() {    // Retrieving from a Map adds a slight overhead compared to direct property access.    // The conditional check here is also often redundant if components are guaranteed to exist.    const engineComponent = this.#components.get('primaryEngine');    return engineComponent ? engineComponent.start() : "Spaceship has no engine to activate!";  }  engageWeapons() {    // Similar to activateThrusters, this adds unnecessary overhead and a redundant check.    const weaponComponent = this.#components.get('offensiveSystem');    return weaponComponent ? weaponComponent.fire() : "Spaceship has no weapon system to engage!";  }}// Example usage:const impulseEngine = new Engine(5000);const laserCannons = new WeaponSystem(120);const starship = new Spaceship(impulseEngine, laserCannons);console.log(starship.activateThrusters());console.log(starship.engageWeapons());
hints.bad_practice: Storing known, fixed components in a Map adds unnecessary indirection and overhead compared to direct property assignment. The conditional checks for component existence at every method call are also redundant if components are guaranteed to be provided during construction.
